title: Design System: Andrew Rix · AI-Native Practice Lead

signal-teal.note: Light value darkened from #0c7f88 (4.18:1) to #00717a (5.05:1) on the light ground. Do not re-lighten.

muted-2.note: Light value darkened from #66798d (3.93:1) to #56687c (5.02:1) on the light ground. Do not re-lighten.

surface-2.note: Lower stop of every surface gradient; needs its own token because light --panel and --ink-2 are both white.

display.purpose: Hero headline only. Capped at 19ch so it always breaks to three lines.

headline.purpose: CTA heading; the sidebar name sits just under it at 1.72rem.

title.purpose: Timeline role headings (--fs-title, 1.25rem). Card titles sit at --fs-lead in Signal Teal.

body.purpose: All prose (--fs-body, 1rem). Lede at --fs-lead/1.7 capped 60ch; timeline paragraphs cap at 70ch.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows, kicker, dates, table headers (--fs-micro, 0.72rem). Always the display family.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Resting state of every large surface. The inset highlight keeps the panel gradient from looking printed.

shadows.name: card-lifted
shadows.purpose: Card hover only, paired with a 4px lift.

shadows.name: glow-teal
shadows.purpose: Lit points: active nav dot, kicker spark, timeline stop centres, progress bar.

shadows.name: glow-violet
shadows.purpose: Violet lit points: AI chip dots, later timeline stops.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: White client logo plates sitting on the dark ground.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Ease-out, no overshoot.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour and border state changes on links, chips, contact rows.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover translate on cards, buttons, plates, badges.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-in reveal: opacity 0 to 1 with a 22px rise. Falls back to visible when the observer or motion preference is absent.

motion.name: bg-wash
motion.purpose: Ambient background gradient drift. Slow enough to be felt, not watched.

motion.name: stream-flow
motion.purpose: Upward fill of the value-stream spine.

motion.name: count-up
motion.value: 1100ms, cubic ease-out, once on first view

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The CTA action. The one place teal and violet are allowed to blend.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The secondary action. Translucent panel fill, teal on hover.

components.name: Skill Chip
components.description: A capability label. Non-interactive by design — a label, not a filter.

components.name: AI Skill Chip
components.description: The violet variant marking the AI-era capabilities. The leading dot is how the skills section shows what is new.

components.name: Highlight Card
components.description: Career-highlight surface. Flat at rest; on hover it lifts and a masked teal hairline fades in around the edge.

narrative.overview:
The system takes its governing metaphor from the work it describes. A career in flow and transformation is drawn as a stream: a single lit spine runs down the experience section, teal shading into violet as the timeline moves from scaled-Agile work into AI, with each role a stop along it. Everything else in the system serves that spine. The near-black ground is not a mood choice, it is the condition that lets a signal read; the ambient wash and 64px grid behind it are the noise floor the signal sits above.

The register is assured, curious, ahead. Two readers use this page: an executive skimming for altitude and a hiring manager reading the record line by line. The system serves both by keeping one strong hierarchy and by never decorating a thing that is not carrying information. A status dot, a pulsing ring, a flowing line, a count-up: each of these is reporting something. Nothing here is ornament dressed as instrumentation.

What the system rejects is stated plainly in PRODUCT.md and holds here. It is not the generic AI landing page, not a LinkedIn profile clone, and not a PDF poured into a browser. If a section could be lifted onto any AI product's launch page without changing a word, it is wrong.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#080f1a) with tonal panels stacked over it; no bright surface anywhere in the dark theme
Two accents only, each with an assigned meaning: teal for signal and position, violet for change and AI
One display family carrying every heading, label and number; one body family carrying prose
Motion that reports state rather than announcing arrival
A complete second theme, not an inverted afterthought: light mode redefines all fifteen tokens
Print is a first-class target — the page is also a CV

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal and violet are the entire accent vocabulary and they are not interchangeable. Teal means this is live, this is where you are, this is the credential. Violet means this is the change, this is the AI end of the story. A third accent is prohibited; Status Green is the one exception and it owns exactly one dot.

rules.name: The No-Bright-Surface Rule
rules.body: In the dark theme, no surface is lighter than #152640. Depth is achieved by stacking tones toward the panel end, never by introducing a light card. The one deliberate exception is client logo plates, which are white because that is what a logo needs to be legible.

rules.name: The Parity Rule
rules.body: Light mode is a full redefinition of all fifteen tokens, not a filter. Any new token added to the dark theme must be given a light value in the same commit, and that value must be measured against the light ground rather than translated by eye.

rules.name: The Display-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Every number, date, credential and label is set in Bricolage, not Plex. The body font handles sentences; the display font handles anything that is a fact.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: No line of prose exceeds 70ch and the hero lede stops at 60ch. Headlines cap by character count rather than percentage, so the break points survive every viewport.

rules.name: The Contact Rule
rules.body: Shadow is a state, not a style. If an element is not hovered, focused or emitting a signal, it has no shadow beyond the ambient card value. Adding a resting drop shadow to make something pop is forbidden; raise its tone instead.

rules.name: The One-Value Rule
rules.body: A size that isn't on the eight-step scale doesn't go in. If a new element seems to need something between two steps, it belongs on one of them.

dos: Do assign meaning before colour. Teal for live/position/credential, violet for change/AI. If a new element does not fit either meaning, it is neutral.
Do set every number, date and label in Bricolage Grotesque and every sentence in IBM Plex Sans.
Do keep prose to 70ch and the hero lede to 60ch.
Do give each new token a light-theme value in the same change.
Do verify contrast at 4.5:1 for anything under 18px, in both themes.
Do keep motion reporting state — a dot that pulses because he is available, a line that flows because it is a stream, a number that counts because it is a total.

Do give every explicit width and height attributes matching the file's intrinsic size, and pair them with width: auto in any CSS rule that sets only height — otherwise the attribute supplies the used width and the image renders squashed.
Do check the print stylesheet after any structural change. The page is also a CV.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: any new animation joins the existing reduce rule.
donts: Don't build anything that reads as a generic AI landing page — gradient orb heroes, glass cards, 'supercharge your workflow' copy, purple-on-black SaaS template.
Don't let it drift toward a LinkedIn profile clone: no endorsement bars, no skill-strength meters, no wall of undifferentiated roles.
Don't let it flatten into a plain PDF resume on the web.
Don't introduce a third accent colour. Two signals, plus one green dot.
Don't place a light or white surface on the dark theme. White is reserved for client logo plates.
Don't add a resting drop shadow to lift an element. Raise its tone toward Panel 2 instead.

Don't gate content visibility on the reveal class. The hidden state lives on .js .reveal, set before first paint, and is backed by reduced-motion, missing-observer, hidden-document and 1200ms watchdog guards.
Don't apply an eyebrow to a new section by reflex. Six already carry one, which is the system's cadence.
Don't re-lighten --teal (#00717a) or --muted-2 (#56687c) in the light theme; both sit just above 5:1 by measurement.
